title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Tech Riptide Before the Turkey
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures are down about two and a half percent as the AI and chip selloff deepens, with the VIX near 29. Traders brace for a big 7:30 AM CT data dump led by October PCE inflation, ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving closure.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: As of about 4:30 AM CT, S&P 500 futures were down 1.5%, Nasdaq-100 futures down 2.5%, Dow futures down 0.8% and Russell 2000 futures down 1.0%; early quotes can shift.
The tech selloff resumed after Tuesday, when the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.5% and the S&P 500 lost 0.5% while the Dow rose 0.9% to its first close above 50,000.
The VIX jumped about 10% to near 29, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased slightly to about 4.90%.
WTI crude slipped to about $81.80 and gold fell about 0.9% to near $3,560; bitcoin dropped about 1.4% to roughly $58,900. A dollar index reading was not available in our sources.
Asia followed Wall Street lower: Japan's Nikkei fell 2.8%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng 1.1% and the Shanghai Composite 2.0%.
Europe was mixed; Germany's final third-quarter GDP came in at 0.1% growth, a touch under forecast.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: October PCE inflation, expected +0.3% for the month and 3.8% from a year ago; core PCE expected +0.3% and 3.2%.
7:30 AM CT: Q3 GDP second estimate, expected 3.5% annualized; also weekly jobless claims (about 200,000 expected), October personal income and spending, and durable goods orders.
9:00 AM CT: October new home sales, expected around 650,000 annualized.
9:30 AM CT: EIA weekly crude oil inventories.
Fed: futures price roughly a 95% to 98% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December; New York Fed President John Williams signaled support for a hike.
Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday is a shortened session.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Dell beat with record quarterly revenue of $54.9 billion, an AI order backlog of $132 billion and a higher full-year forecast; shares rose after hours.
Ambarella beat on profit but guided next-quarter revenue far below expectations, blaming memory costs; shares sank more than 35% after hours.
Workday, Autodesk and Nutanix all beat estimates but fell after hours on soft or cautious guidance; Nutanix also announced its CEO will step down.
Urban Outfitters posted record third-quarter sales, but weak Anthropologie trends sent shares down about 11% after hours.
HP Inc. beat and gave an upbeat outlook, and shares rose after hours.
Deere and Li Auto report before today's open; a Benzinga headline says Li Auto shares were up about 5% premarket.
With the holiday ahead, after-close reports today are light.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): about -5% — the slide continues after Tuesday's near-6% drop, amid AI profitability doubts and political fallout around CEO Jensen Huang.
AMBA (Ambarella): sharply lower, more than -35% after hours — weak revenue guidance tied to rising memory prices.
URBN (Urban Outfitters): about -11% after hours — soft Anthropologie results overshadowed record sales.
NTNX (Nutanix): about -8% after hours — weak full-year guidance and a CEO transition.
WDAY (Workday): about -7% after hours — soft subscription guidance despite a beat.
ADSK (Autodesk): about -4% after hours — fell despite a beat and solid guidance.
DELL (Dell Technologies): higher after hours — record revenue and a huge AI server backlog.
LI (Li Auto): about +5% premarket per Benzinga — reported results this morning.

sections.title: Business News
items: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion; Insmed jumped 14% Tuesday.
Anthropic shares closed below their $83 IPO price for the first time on Tuesday.
Reports say Blackstone, Warburg Pincus and Apollo are in talks to back a roughly $50 billion buyout of Global Payments led by GTCR.
Natural gas futures surged about 15% Tuesday on a cold snap, while oil got a lift from attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.
Shein agreed to pay $100 million to settle FTC claims.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT: the PCE inflation and GDP data dump, which could firm up or soften bets on a December Fed hike.
Whether Nvidia and the chip names find a floor at the 8:30 AM CT open after two straight days of heavy selling.
Holiday liquidity: volume may thin out into the afternoon ahead of Thursday's closure.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, November twenty-fifth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Sitting next to me in the cabana is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, who already smells the Thanksgiving turkey. Give the crew a holiday hello, Gus! Okay, Trade Wind surfers, conditions on the dawn patrol are choppy. We're calling it Poor. There's a tech riptide pulling hard this morning. As of about four thirty A M Central, Nasdaq futures were down about two and a half percent. S and P futures were off one and a half percent. Dow futures were down almost one percent, and the Russell was down about one percent. Those are early quotes, so they could shift. Yesterday the Dow closed above fifty thousand for the first time, but tech wiped out. The fear gauge, the VIX, jumped to about twenty-nine. That's gnarly. The ten-year yield eased to about four point nine percent. Crude is near eighty-two dollars. Gold and bitcoin are both lower. Asia followed Wall Street down, with Japan's Nikkei off almost three percent. Europe was mixed. Now the weather. At seven thirty A M Central we get a big set all at once. October P C E inflation, expected at three point eight percent from a year ago. Plus the second look at third quarter GDP, jobless claims, and durable goods. Traders already see a December rate hike as nearly locked in. A hot number could make the wind even rougher. On the tide chart, Dell crushed it. Record revenue, a giant AI order backlog, and a higher forecast. Dell caught a clean wave after hours. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Not everyone was so lucky. Ambarella wiped out, down more than thirty-five percent after hours on weak guidance. Workday, Autodesk, and Nutanix all beat, but slipped on cautious outlooks. Urban Outfitters fell about eleven percent. And Nvidia, the Kahuna of chips, is down about five percent more before the bell. Deere and Li Auto report this morning. In beach talk, Sanofi is buying Insmed for about forty-one billion dollars. And Anthropic dipped below its IPO price for the first time. Sets to watch today: the seven thirty data, whether chips find a floor at the open, and thin holiday trading. Remember, markets are closed tomorrow for Thanksgiving, and Friday is a short session. Soul surfers, no need to drop in on every wave today. Want me to call a wave for you? Type any stock, E T F, or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will read the surf for you. Happy Thanksgiving, everybody! This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
